summary: Read-mostly workspace audit command that surveys git worktrees, plan slugs, active-plan registry, claim locks, uncommitted work, and follow-up entries; cross-references them into a single consistency report with six sections and four cross-reference boolean flags. Default run is zero mutations; every cleanup action (prune-worktrees / archive-plans / clean-locks / reap-registry / open-followups) is opt-in per-flag with AskUserQuestion per-item confirmation. Classification logic lives in scripts/reconcile.py (testable, no I/O); command body is a thin orchestrator.

flags.description: Removes worktrees classified 'dead' only; per-item AskUserQuestion before each git worktree remove.
Moves plans classified 'precontext-only-aged' or 'stale-in-progress' to <base>/plans/.abandoned/<slug>/; writes RECONCILE-ARCHIVED.md sentinel; never touches 'tasks-complete-unmerged' plans.
Removes claim locks when all three conditions hold: plan-claim.sh reap-stale reports free/stale/corrupt AND no live registry record AND daemon PID not alive. Never calls rm without reap-stale check.
Deregisters stale registry records individually via active-plan-registry.py deregister --run-id. Never calls the global reap subcommand.
Creates follow-up entries via sink-add.sh for 'tasks-complete-unmerged' plans; idempotent via content_hash dedup.
Writes the Phase 1 report to RECONCILE.md at repo root, or to the optional positional <save-path> argument. Without --save, only stdout output.

worktree_classes.description: Clean working tree, no unpushed commits, HEAD is commit-ancestry ancestor of default branch. The only class offered for auto-prune.
HEAD is detached; no branch reference. Manual review required. Always surface-only.
Branch appears merged via squash or ambiguous evidence (e.g. commit subject contains '(#…)'). Always surface-only.
Remote unreachable; unpushed-commit check skipped. Always surface-only.
No evidence worktree is safe to prune; default for anything not matching the above.

plan_classes.description: Only INTENT/precontext artifacts present (no TASKS.md/LEDGER.md/events.jsonl) and past the 14-day staleness threshold.
All TASKS.md lines are [x] but no merge/commit evidence found. Advisory only; never auto-archived; offered as follow-up via --open-followups.
Plan has recent activity and tasks; no other class applies. No action recommended.
In-progress plan that has been inactive for >14 days (staleness threshold). Archivable with --archive-plans.

cross_reference_flags.description: At least one worktree's branch is merged into the default branch but is still on disk and not classified 'dead'.
At least one plan has all tasks [x] but no merge/commit evidence.
At least one claim lock has no matching live registry record.
At least one plan slug has uncommitted file changes attributed to it via plan path overlap.

safety_model.default_run: zero mutations — no file written, no lock removed, no worktree pruned, no plan moved, no registry record deleted, no follow-up created
safety_model.per_item_confirm: every mutation fires AskUserQuestion individually; batch confirmation not permitted
safety_model.dead_only_prune: only 'dead'-classified worktrees offered for prune; dirty/detached/merged-uncertain/unknown-remote/active are surface-only unconditionally
safety_model.lock_removal_policy: all three conditions must hold: reap-stale reports free|stale|corrupt AND no live registry record AND daemon PID not alive; rm never called without reap-stale
safety_model.never_deletes_plan_artifacts: archiving moves directory contents; INTENT.md/SPEC.md/TASKS.md/LEDGER.md always preserved
safety_model.abandoned_excluded: plans under <base>/plans/.abandoned/ excluded from slug scans; RECONCILE-ARCHIVED.md sentinel marks recognized archived plans
safety_model.never_rm_live_lock: a lock whose daemon PID is alive is never removed regardless of reap-stale output
safety_model.registry_unavailable: if registry errors or is absent, prints '(registry unavailable)' and continues; robust to missing infrastructure
safety_model.tasks_complete_never_archived: tasks-complete-unmerged plans are never offered for --archive-plans; advisory only

save_convention.positional_override: passing a non-flag positional argument implies --save and overrides the path

staleness_threshold.staleness_signal: max(latest events.jsonl timestamp for slug, artifact mtime) — not raw directory age

invariants: Default run is zero mutations — no flag means read-only report only.
Only 'dead' worktrees are auto-prune-eligible; all other classes are surface-only unconditionally.
Lock removal requires all three conditions: reap-stale free|stale|corrupt + no live registry record + daemon PID not alive.
tasks-complete-unmerged plans are never auto-archived; they are advisory only.
archiving moves plan directory (never deletes); INTENT.md/SPEC.md/TASKS.md/LEDGER.md always preserved in destination.
Global active-plan-registry.py reap is never called; per-item deregistration only via deregister --run-id.
Default branch resolved dynamically via git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD; never hardcoded.
Plans under <base>/plans/.abandoned/ are excluded from slug scans.
No subagent dispatch; no LLM calls; shell + Python only.
Classification logic lives in scripts/reconcile.py; command body is a thin orchestrator.
gotchas: merged_worktree_on_disk flag does NOT trigger for 'dead' worktrees — those are already on the --prune-worktrees path; the flag surfaces merged worktrees blocked by other conditions (dirty+merged, etc.).
unknown-remote classification fires when has_unpushed is None for ANY reason, not just remote failure — safety-conservative: if the check was skipped, treat as surface-only.
staleness uses latest_activity_ts (max of events.jsonl mtime and artifact mtimes), NOT directory creation or modification date.
tasks-complete-unmerged is advisory only even when --archive-plans is passed — it is never offered for archiving.
plan-claim.sh reap-stale exit codes: 0=held, 1=free, 2=stale, 3=corrupt; only 1/2/3 can lead toward lock removal (all three conditions still required).
RECONCILE-ARCHIVED.md sentinel written by --archive-plans is how subsequent /z-reconcile runs recognize archived plans and skip them.
The report's Follow-ups section is always rendered even without --open-followups; it shows advisory findings. The flag only controls whether entries are actually created.
